subject.title: iOS remote pairing UX: QR crash, onboarding paste fails, Settings paste works (cellular); feedback on edge auth + mobile wss://

question: Should OpenClaw document a supported split-host public exposure pattern where browser/operator access stays behind SSO/OIDC while a separate mobile `wss://` hostname uses OpenClaw token plus device-pair bootstrap auth?
rationale: The remaining request defines a public Gateway exposure boundary and mobile bootstrap-auth path, so automation should not decide the supported security posture or limits.

options.title: Document Split-Host Mobile Pairing
options.body: Add a security-reviewed advanced recipe that keeps Tailscale Serve as the default while documenting a dedicated mobile `wss://` hostname, no browser SSO redirect on that host, token/device bootstrap auth, `trustedProxies`, and validation steps.

options.title: Keep Generic Exposure Guidance
options.body: Treat split public mobile pairing as operator-managed advanced setup and leave docs focused on Tailscale Serve, trusted-proxy auth, and general exposure warnings.

options.title: Defer Public Mobile Pairing Direction
options.body: Keep this issue open until maintainers decide whether public mobile pairing beyond Tailscale Serve should be a first-class supported deployment shape.

recommendation.title: Document Split-Host Mobile Pairing
recommendation.body: Add a security-reviewed advanced recipe that keeps Tailscale Serve as the default while documenting a dedicated mobile `wss://` hostname, no browser SSO redirect on that host, token/device bootstrap auth, `trustedProxies`, and validation steps.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete owns the most recent route-list fix and adjacent iOS gateway handoff history, making them the strongest available owner for the public mobile pairing trust-boundary decision.
